questions.learningObjective: apply the doctrine of negligence duty and breach to a concrete legal fact pattern
questions.stem: Consider this: A shopper injured by a spill sues the owner for negligence. The hazard existed for two hours. Which statement best states the governing legal rule?

options.text: A duty exists whenever someone is injured, regardless of the relationship or foreseeability in this situation.
options.misconception: assumes duty follows from every injury

options.text: No duty is owed unless the parties signed an agreement for this case.
If the defendant was careless, a duty automatically exists in the circumstances.

A person generally owes a duty of reasonable care to those whose conduct creates a foreseeable risk of harm, and the duty is owed to the class of persons the risk reasonably threatens as applied here.

questions.explanation: Duty is a limit on liability. It asks whether the plaintiff was within the foreseeable zone of risk created by the defendant's conduct, so that the law will recognize an obligation to take care. Here the decisive point is the existence of a duty of reasonable care, so the result follows from that doctrine rather than from the surface appeal of a competing statement. Each distractor rests on a different mistake about how the doctrine operates.
questions.hint: Ask whether the plaintiff was a foreseeable victim of the defendant's conduct. Keep the inquiry on the existence of a duty of reasonable care.
